tasks.title: M4 Component ceilings: ingest, ClickHouse queries, workers, PostgreSQL (R19)
tasks.note: Ceilings measured (docs/scale-tests.md, Phase 11 component ceilings). Ingest: 5x held with readers off; 10x crossed on points only, the Collector metrics exporter flat at ~90k points/s with its queue full and ClickHouse at 2.3 cores. Search at 1x: 8/s held (p95 614 ms), 16/s collapsed (unbounded concurrency, 428 queries at once, ingest lost ~40 % of points). Workers: 1x and 2x (100 rules/100 SLOs) held; at 4x (200/200) platform-api segfaulted (exit 139) in the burst of 102 SLO burn alerts after PostgreSQL refused connections (53300 too many clients); core dump taken, not analysed. Reviewed (two rounds, 21 fixes, confirmation clean). The workers ceiling at 4x is unmeasured: the crash is first in milestone 5.

tasks.title: M5 Fixes: ingest path, ClickHouse isolation, queries, PostgreSQL if needed (R11, R12, R12a, R12b)
tasks.note: One change at a time, before and after; final rerun with held-out 4x/6x for the ±25 % check. 1, the crash: the local channel ran a handler per alert transition with no bound (Juice LocalChannelOptions.MaxConcurrency unset), now 8 (Messaging:Local:MaxConcurrency); platform-api restart: unless-stopped; the harness counts restarts as a crash. Core dump read (dotnet-dump, Alpine SDK container): the segfault is in Npgsql's GSS encryption probe (native GSSAPI InitSecContext, two threads at once) on new physical connections in the burst, not in the 53300 path; GSS Encryption Mode now Disable unless the connection string sets it (PlatformDbContext.WithoutGssProbe). Verified at workers 4x (docs/scale-tests.md, Phase 11 fixes): with the bound alone no burst happened (SLOs already in the database); with both and COPY_FROM=5 (150 new SLOs) the burst came (142 burn alerts resolved in one pass, then 24 fired) and every line held, no restart. SLO watermark newest first (2 min, then 15) and presence from spans and logs first (metrics only for uncovered minutes); 4x rerun (20261115T1129): SLO worker 0.382 to 0.111 cores, every reader query 0.955 to 0.569; container median 0.47 to 0.42, p90 2.29 to 1.85, mean 0.87 to 1.07 (top-1 % bursts of 8-12 cores, unexplained). no 53300. Also a midnight-UTC test bug fixed in SloTests. R11 step 1 (per-query settings, plus a bound): the API's ClickHouse queries at most ClickHouse:Api:MaxConcurrent (8) per replica, waiting QueueTimeout (5 s), each with max_execution_time 20 and max_threads 2; refused, cut (159/202/241) or unreachable is 503 "Busy, try again" / "unavailable" with Retry-After (also closes the milestone 2 gap: 500 while ClickHouse is down). Measured (20261115T0202/0235): 8/s p95 314 ms (was 614); 16/s degrades instead of collapsing: all ingest stored (was 64.8 % of points), ClickHouse memory 3.7 GiB (was 22.8), 14.1 searches/s answered at p50 5.4 s, 3,308 of 28,777 refused with 503 busy. Step 2 (workload scheduling) deferred to the final full-mix rerun. R12, searches newest slice first: trace and log searches read the newest 5 min, then 1 h, 12 h, the window, until a page is full (exact; one slot for all slices). Isolated on the 16/s run's data: log search 3.63 M rows / 0.35 CPU-s to 0.42 M / 0.09; trace search 1.66 M / 0.47 to 0.52 M / 0.16; bounding the second trace scan by otel_traces_trace_id_ts read more, dropped. First run (20261115T0626/0659): 8/s p95 138 ms (was 314), ClickHouse 1.7 cores (was 3.3); 16/s p50 76 ms (was 5.4 s), ClickHouse 5.0 cores (was 15.7), 1,716 refused (was 3,308), all in 07:27:45-07:31:30, when a merge folded the newest minutes into a 10 M-row logs part and each log slice read 3 M rows: the logs table is ordered by toStartOfFiveMinutes(Timestamp) first and ClickHouse does not derive that bound from Timestamp. Fixed with an explicit toStartOfFiveMinutes bound (same slice over the merged part: 3.1 M rows / 1 CPU-s to 0.5 M / 0.1). Rerun (20261115T0739/0813): 8/s p95 119 ms, ClickHouse 1.6 cores; 16/s p50/p95 78/148 ms, 0 of 28,777 refused, ClickHouse 3.1 cores, all ingest stored; a 2.5 M-row logs merge at 08:40 inside the step, log slices at most 0.46 M rows. Discovery (owner chose the slower metrics cadence): resource read 13.6 M rows / 15.5 CPU-s a pass, otel_metrics_sum nearly all of it, cost is the ResourceAttributes map, no rewrite helps; the metric tables now on their own checkpoint every Discovery:MetricsInterval (5 min). 8/s rerun (20261115T0904): discovery 0.52 to 0.16 cores, platform_reader 1.34 to 0.98 (query_log); container CPU unchanged (1.56/1.58), the rest unattributed. Health remembers liveness across passes (Health:LivenessOverlap 1 min). Workers 4x rerun (20261115T1006 against 0019): platform_reader 1.84 to 0.95 cores, ClickHouse container 1.77 to 0.87 mean; discovery 0.58 to 0.18, health 0.32 to 0.12; every line held, no restart. R12a: Collector num_consumers 4 to 16 (every exporter); ingest 10x (20261115T1230 against 1304) points stored 86.5 % to 100 %, 0 lost, queue median 195k to 37k, ClickHouse 1.8 to 1.9 cores; 20x (1338) 55.1 %, about 110k points/s, 4.4 of 16 inserts in flight, so the next limit is in the Collector (not profiled). Queued after R12a (owner, 15 November): measure a materialised TenantId column (LowCardinality, from ResourceAttributes juice.platform_tenant_id, new data only, no MATERIALIZE COLUMN mutation) on a copy of a scale table, map filter against column on the same worker and search queries; ship in 1.3.0 with init scripts and row policies if worth it. Measured (docs/scale-tests.md 8): 380 sampled worker queries replayed on an hour copied from 20261115T1129, results equal; tenant column alone -37 % CPU, plus namespace and environment -49 % (rules -76 %, SLOs -86 %), every worker key -72 %. Owner (16 November): materialise every worker key, but measure the ingest cost first (higher priority); insert cost at 10x ingest (20261116T0141 without, 0216 with the 12 columns, dropped after): +0.29 cores inserts, +0.08 flushes, +0.34 merges, container mean 2.41 to 3.13; insert p50 +11 ms; parts +4 %. Against about 0.4 cores saved on reads at 1x (0.07 added). Both runs lost about 1.5 % of points (baseline a harness limit), not the columns. Shipped (owner, 16 November): clickhouse/resource-columns.sh via a clickhouse-columns service after the Collector (API and Grafana wait), every platform query on the columns (ResourceColumns), grafana_tenant on JuiceTenant, verify.sh and 3 tests; working stack applied, fresh install simulated; 724 tests pass. Effect for the final rerun. Final rerun (fresh scale stack, 20261116T0442-1x … 0739-10x, docs/scale-tests.md, Phase 11 final rerun): 1× meets every target, every line holds at 3×, 4× and 5× (baseline crossed at 5×); platform reads at 1× 1.90 → 0.28 ClickHouse cores, search p95 292 → 62 ms. 6× dropped 12,948 points once (a 40 s ClickHouse burst: big merges + inserts + discovery); 10× drops 5.8 % of points with ClickHouse at 7 of 24 cores: insert wait 70 → 206 ms caps the 16-consumer metrics export near 95k points/s (next limit; cause of the wait to profile). ±25 % check needs the capacity view (milestone 6); CPU-line preview: 4× −1 %, 6× −25 %; the knee is the export path, not CPU. Review loop (R16): round 1, 10 findings, all fixed (1b5c38b): health liveness widened by how far the newest remembered row trails (ingest backlog lost every row past ~100 s), ID searches in one slice, plain-text 503 when no problem writer, pod filter on columns, column-name test, slot helper, SignalOf shared, ClickHouse:Api validation names the setting, metrics windows reported. Round 2, 10 findings, 5 fixed (22f4dd4): whole liveness read every Health:LivenessFullRead (2 min) for one late-only service (long spans), metrics checkpoint due when missing (InitialLookback < MetricsInterval never ran), negative overlap as none, signals guard, ResourceSelect rename; 5 kept with reasons (slices bounded at 4, 159/241 as busy by R11 design, policy order fine in compose, column test covers renames, slot timing duplicate). Confirmation round, 8 findings: whole read merges instead of clearing (a capped read dropped resources), timer reset on any whole read, a test that depended on other tests' rows fixed, docs: reads ~5 a row (was 3, 10 before Phase 11) and the lateness bound less Lag and a pass; kept: double checkpoint read, metrics checkpoint not seeded from the main (one-time 1 h read on upgrade), no LivenessFullRead validation (documented). 728 tests pass. Milestone 5 done; next milestone 6 (Overview panel, capacity view calibrated on 20261116 1/3/5/10, held-out 4/6).

tasks.title: M6 Overview platform panel and capacity view (R8-R9)
tasks.note: Built from the final rerun (not provisional). Knee model (owner, 16 November): the conservative bracket, since the 6x crossing came from a burst (inserts in flight saturate near 10.5: 10x mean 10.3, 6x p99 10.5 vs 5x 2.8) and interpolating 1/3/5/10 predicts ~9.5-10x (+60 %). Bracket: held to 5x, crossed at 10x; 5x vs measured 6x = -17 %, within +-25 %; held-out 4x held, 6x crossed. Built: /api/v1/platform/overview (operators of this deployment) and the Console Overview's Platform panel (workers with how busy, backlogs, ingestion per signal and export queues from the Collector's :8888 page, ClickHouse CPU against cores, insert p95 and inserts in flight, reads p95 by caller, disk with a day, need at retention and days until full) and capacity view (load multiple per signal, mix, bracket, each resource now against the held and crossed steps; labelled, utilisation only on another machine). Heartbeats carry a moving-mean pass time (migration WorkerPassSeconds); tenants list says canOperate so a viewer never asks; scale/calibration.mjs (steps.sh writes build/scale/calibration-<time>.json, HELD_OUT), components.mjs adds inserts in flight; deploy/local/capacity/calibration.json shipped. Tests: 11 overview tests, 739 pass; e2e/platform.mjs passes (panel, viewer none, health lease held from psql red as unheld in 45 s, green after). Review loop (R16): round 1, 14 findings, all fixed (42f33d2): a full exporter queue judged against its own bound (the calibrated queue is the sum, so it never went red), the panel keeps polling after a failed read, Overview-only ClickHouse reads apart and lighter, days until full only while the tables outgrow the free space, CPU falls back to shares, bad calibration cached and logged once, missing sections rejected, calibration matched by ClickHouse's own cores (file regenerated), harness-problem steps excluded, pass time reset on a retaken lease, shared formatBytes. Round 2, 10 findings, all fixed (0c7f334): a deadline in the Overview reads leaves ClickHouse up, callers once a minute, mix counts apart from the PostgreSQL up statement, cores/memory reread every 10 min, yesterday scaled when its rows span less than a day, canOperate as the endpoint judges it, stop polling on 403, disk and label wording, one CPU rule, no queue figure as 0. Confirmation, 8 findings: 1 false alarm (min_time/max_time are set for the exporter's DateTime64 tables: checked live, now a test assertion), 7 fixed: stale callers dropped on failure and on ClickHouse down, mix unknown until read (not 0), "no estimate yet" for the disk, the label tells unsampled from unreadable cores or memory, a new tenant answer restarts polling, comments. 744 tests pass; e2e/platform.mjs passes. Milestone 6 done; next milestone 7 (sizing guide R18, gate, 1.3.0).

tasks.title: M7 Sizing guide, gate, 1.3.0 (R18)
tasks.note: Started 2026-11-16: deployment.md Sizing and scaling (R18: what one machine carries 1x-10x, what scales out, the six leased workers and their switches, levers, each panel figure to its action, calibrating on another machine; replaces the replicas section that named three workers); version 1.3.0; docs/phase-11-acceptance.md (gate lines to evidence); a gate-2 test (overview answers at once with ClickHouse hanging); tests/upgrade-drill.sh (api-1.2.0 installed, 10 min of 1x, upgraded in place to HEAD: init.sh, compose up, apply-clickhouse-access.sh; checks nothing lost, migrations, columns on old parts, row policy, platform_monitor, platform pipeline, heartbeats, /health/platform). Drill run twice: the first failed only its migration check (wrong history table name, __ef_migrations_history); fixed, rerun build/upgrade-drill-20261116T1151: every check passed, 600,027 spans and all records kept, migrations 19 to 21, 52 s to upgrade; docs/drills.md, runbook Upgrade rewritten to the drilled steps. 745 tests pass. Review loop (R16): round 1, 10 findings, all fixed (cffd8de): the drill can't run outside its worktree (an unchecked cd could have rewritten the working .env), removes an earlier drill project, a missing count is lost, every platform table counted, migrations against the release's files, a failed load or access script fails it, the old traces read through the new columns by the upgraded API (the column comparison couldn't fail); gate-2 test's accept loop thread-safe; MODIFY TTL advice. Round 2, 10 findings, 9 fixed (34aa398): every enabled worker passing, leak check by the reported service names, a non-numeric before count fails, ports checked whoever holds them, one psql call, warm-up before the gate-2 timing, the acceptance command; kept: shared counting with restore-drill (they count different things). Confirmation, 8 findings, all fixed: ports read from the compose file and checked before anything is removed (with a 1 s timeout), each table counted alone if the one query fails, all 8 workers with each replica's row judged alone, psql helper reused. Drill runs 3 to 5 passed (record build/upgrade-drill-20261116T1308: 13 of 13 checks, 36 s compose up). Milestone 7 done.
